p.src: Now Grandee Wu Li appointed the princess Qiongying as his vanguard and followed behind at the head of the main army. Qiongying was only sixteen, a maiden whose beauty rivaled the flowers, and was not in fact Wu Li's own daughter. Her true family name was Qiu; her father was named Shen, and their ancestral home was at Mianshang in Jiexiu County, Fenyang Prefecture. This Mianshang was the very place that Duke Wen of Jin, in the Spring and Autumn period, granted as a fief to Jie Zhitui after failing to find him. Qiu Shen possessed considerable property and had reached the age of fifty, yet still had no heir. After losing his wife, he married as his second wife the daughter of Song Youlie of Pingyao County, and she bore Qiongying. When the girl was ten, Song Youlie died, whereupon Lady Song accompanied her husband Qiu Shen to attend her father's funeral. Pingyao bordered Jiexiu and lay a little over seventy li away. Because the journey was long and their departure hurried, Lady Song left Qiongying at home and instructed the steward Ye Qing and his wife to watch over and attend her. She and her husband were midway through their journey when a band of outlaws suddenly appeared, killed Qiu Shen, scattered the household retainers, and carried Lady Song away. The retainers fled home and reported the news to Ye Qing. Though Ye Qing was only a steward, he possessed a strong sense of honor and was also skilled with spear and staff. His wife, Lady An, was a most prudent woman. Ye Qing immediately informed the Qiu clan, while on the one hand reporting the crime to the authorities and seeking the outlaws' arrest, and on the other burying his master's body. The Qiu clansmen resolved to appoint a man of their own lineage to inherit the family estate. Ye Qing and his wife, Lady An, cared for their young mistress Qiongying.

p.src: A little over a year later, Tian Hu rose in rebellion and seized Weisheng. He sent Wu Li with a detachment to raid the countryside. When they reached Mianshang in Jiexiu, they plundered property and carried off men and women; the Qiu family's adopted heir was killed by the marauding soldiers, while Ye Qing, his wife, and the girl Qiongying were all taken captive. Wu Li likewise had no heir. Seeing Qiongying's delicate features and clear eyes, he brought her to meet his wife, Lady Ni. Lady Ni had never borne a child, and the moment she saw Qiongying she loved her dearly, treating her just like her own daughter. Qiongying had been clever and quick-witted from childhood. Realizing that she could not escape alive from that place, and having no kin to turn to, she saw that Lady Ni loved her and asked her to obtain Ye Qing's wife, Lady An, from Wu Li and bring her in. Thus Lady An was able to remain constantly at Qiongying's side. When Ye Qing was captured, he had wanted to escape, but then he thought, “Qiongying is still young, and she is the only flesh and blood left by my master and mistress. If I go, I shall never know whether she lives or dies. Fortunately my wife is with her. If some opportunity arises and I can deliver them both from this calamity, my master will be able to close his eyes in peace beneath the Nine Springs.” For that reason, he had no choice but to submit to Wu Li. After Ye Qing distinguished himself in battle, Wu Li returned Lady An to him. From then on, Lady An could enter and leave the commander's residence and exchange news with Qiongying. Wu Li also petitioned Tian Hu, who appointed Ye Qing a chief administrator.

p.src: Later, Wu Li sent Ye Qing to Mount Shishi to quarry timber and stone. The soldiers under him pointed beneath a ridge and said, “There is a beautiful stone here, as white as frost and snow, without the slightest flaw. The local people tried to quarry it, but a thunderclap struck them, frightening several stonecutters senseless; it was a long while before they revived. Since then, everyone has bitten a finger and warned one another, and none dares approach it.” Hearing this, Ye Qing went with the soldiers to look beneath the ridge. The men all cried out together, “How strange! Just now it was plainly a white stone—how has it suddenly turned into a woman's corpse?” Ye Qing stepped forward and examined it closely. Strange beyond belief, it was the body of his mistress, Lady Song. Her face still seemed alive, while the wounds upon her head and face looked as though she had fallen from the ridge and been dashed to death. Ye Qing wept in astonishment, not knowing what to make of it. Then a soldier in his unit, formerly one of Tian Hu's mounted attendants, related every detail of how Lady Song had been abducted and died: “When the Great King first raised his army, he seized this woman in the region of Jiexiu and intended to make her his stronghold wife. The woman tricked the Great King into untying her bonds, and when they reached this place, she hurled herself from the high ridge and was dashed to death. When the Great King saw that she was dead, he ordered me down the ridge to strip off her clothes and ornaments. It was I who attended her onto the horse, and I who stripped off her clothes, so I remember her face clearly. There can be no doubt whatsoever that this is she. More than three years have now passed; how can her body still be perfectly preserved?” When Ye Qing had heard him out, he swallowed all his boundless tears and said to the soldiers, “I too recognize her unmistakably. She is the daughter of old Song, who was once my neighbor.” Ye Qing ordered the soldiers to bring earth to cover the body, but when he stepped forward to look, it had become a white stone once more. The men marveled and sighed deeply, then went about their stone-quarrying work. When the work was done, Ye Qing returned to Weisheng and had Lady An secretly tell Qiongying how Tian Hu had killed Qiu Shen and abducted Lady Song, and how Lady Song had preserved her chastity by hurling herself to her death.

p.src: When Qiongying learned the news, it was as though ten thousand arrows pierced her heart. Day and night she stifled her sobs and wept, shedding pearl-like tears in secret, and never for an instant forgot her desire to avenge her parents. From then on, whenever she closed her eyes at night, a divine figure appeared and said, “If you wish to avenge your parents, let me teach you the martial arts.” Qiongying was intelligent and quick by nature, and remembered everything upon waking. She would quietly take up a staff, bolt her chamber door, and practice inside. As the days passed, she became highly accomplished in the martial arts. Before she knew it, the last winter month of the fourth year of Xuanhe had arrived. One evening, while Qiongying dozed with her head resting on the table, she suddenly heard a gust of wind and caught an unearthly fragrance. Suddenly she saw a refined scholar wearing a folded-corner cap, who brought with him a young general in a green robe and had him teach Qiongying to strike targets with flying stones. The scholar also said to Qiongying, “I made a special journey to Gaoping and invited the ‘Star of Heavenly Swiftness’ here to teach you his extraordinary art, deliver you from the tiger's den, and enable you to avenge your parents. This general is also your destined husband from a former life.” At the words “destined husband from a former life,” Qiongying blushed so deeply she wished the ground would swallow her, and hurriedly covered her face with her sleeve. As soon as she moved her hand, however, she knocked the scissors on the table, making them ring sharply. She awoke with a start. The cold moon and dying lamp were still before her eyes; it had seemed a dream, yet not a dream. Qiongying sat motionless, lost in thought for a long while, before at last going to rest.

p.src: The next day, Qiongying still remembered the method of casting flying stones. She picked up an egg-sized round stone by the wall and, without judging the height or distance, tried hurling it at the ornamental owl-tail on the ridge of her chamber roof. It struck squarely with a loud crash, shattering the ornament to pieces that scattered all over the ground. The noise startled Lady Ni, who hurried over to ask what had happened. Qiongying cleverly dissembled, saying, “Last night I dreamed that a divine figure told me: ‘Your father is destined to become a prince or marquis, so I have come especially to teach you extraordinary arts and martial skills, that you may help your father achieve success.’ Just now I tried casting a stone, never imagining that it would strike the owl-tail squarely.” Lady Ni was astonished and reported the whole story to Wu Li. Wu Li could hardly believe it. He immediately summoned Qiongying and questioned her, then tested her with spear, saber, sword, halberd, cudgel, staff, fork, and rake; sure enough, she had mastered every one of them. She also possessed the skill of casting flying stones and could hit the mark every time. Wu Li was amazed and thought, “I am truly blessed! Heaven has bestowed an extraordinary person upon me as my aid.” From then on, he had Qiongying spend each day training, galloping horses and practicing with the sword.

Seeing that Qiongying’s condition was too difficult to meet, Wu Li let the matter of choosing a husband drop. Now, however, the thought of becoming a prince or marquis stirred treacherous ambitions in Wu Li. He therefore recommended Qiongying as vanguard, intending to profit from the conflict between the two sides. Wu Li then selected his soldiers and officers and departed from Weisheng. He assigned five thousand picked troops to Qiongying as vanguard, while he himself commanded the main army and advanced behind her.

p.src: Leaving Wu Li and Qiongying to advance their army, let us speak instead of Song Jiang and the others at Zhaode, awaiting the arrival of Pacification Commissioner Chen. More than ten days passed before word finally came that Commissioner Chen and his troops had arrived. Song Jiang led his generals far beyond the city walls to welcome him, then escorted him into Zhaode Prefecture to lodge there, which was provisionally made the field headquarters. All the generals and commanders came to pay their respects, and the formal courtesies were completed. Though Commissioner Chen had long known of Song Jiang and his companions’ loyalty and righteousness, he had never had occasion to meet Song Jiang face-to-face. Now, seeing how modest, courteous, benevolent, and generous he was, Chen esteemed him all the more and said, “His Majesty knows that the Vanguard has repeatedly won extraordinary victories and has specially dispatched this humble official to supervise here. I have also brought cartloads of gold, silver, and silks bestowed as rewards.” Song Jiang and the others bowed in thanks and said, “Through Your Excellency’s vigorous recommendation on our behalf, we have today received such abundant imperial favor; it is all due to your benevolence. Above us we receive the Son of Heaven’s grace, and below we are grateful for Your Excellency’s virtue. Even if Song Jiang and his companions were to have their livers and brains smeared upon the ground, we could never repay you.” Commissioner Chen said, “General, win great merit soon and return triumphantly to the capital. The Son of Heaven will surely entrust you with high office.” Song Jiang bowed twice more in thanks and said, “May I trouble Your Excellency to hold Zhaode while I divide my forces to seize Tian Hu’s lair, leaving him unable to support either his front or his rear.” Commissioner Chen said, “Before leaving the capital, I already memorialized His Majesty. For the prefectures and counties recently won by the Vanguard that now lack magistrates, the responsible ministry has been ordered to appoint replacements without delay and require them to set out by a fixed deadline. They will arrive within a few days.” On the one hand, Song Jiang distributed the imperial rewards among the officers and men; on the other, he wrote military dispatches and sent Dai Zong, the “Magic Courier,” to deliver orders to the commanders guarding the various prefectures, departments, and counties: as soon as the new officials arrived, they were to hand over their posts and bring their troops to await assignment. After conveying the orders throughout the prefectures and departments, Dai Zong was to proceed to Fenyang, reconnoiter the military situation, and return with a report. Song Jiang also submitted to Commissioner Chen an account of the achievements of Tang Bin and the other surrendered generals from Hebei. He then recommended Jin Ding and Huang Yue to guard Huguan and Baodu, replacing Sun Li, Zhu Tong, and the other officers so that the latter could come and serve under his command. Commissioner Chen approved every proposal.

p.src: Suddenly, a scout came galloping in like a shooting star and reported, “Tian Hu has sent Ma Ling to command officers and troops to relieve Fenyang; he has also sent Imperial Kinsman Wu Li and Princess Qiongying with officers and troops, and they have struck eastward as far as Xiangyuan.” When Song Jiang heard this, he conferred with Wu Yong and assigned generals to meet the enemy. At this, the surrendered general Qiao Daoqing said, “Ma Ling has long possessed sorcery and also knows the art of magic travel. He conceals golden bricks upon his person and strikes men with them, never missing his mark. Since the Vanguard took this humble Taoist into his service, I have yet to exert myself. I ask to go to Fenyang with my master, Gongsun Yiqing, and persuade Ma Ling to surrender.” Song Jiang was delighted and immediately assigned two thousand troops for Gongsun Sheng and Qiao Daoqing to lead there. The two took leave of Song Jiang and set out with the troops that very day, heading for Fenyang. We shall say no more of them for now.

p.src: The advance scouts under Wang Ying had already reached the northern side of Mount Wuyin, within the borders of Xiangyuan County, when they encountered the northern generals Ye Qing and Sheng Ben, who had come out to reconnoiter. The two forces collided, beating their drums and waving their banners. The northern general Sheng Ben reined his horse before the ranks. Wang Ying galloped out from the Song formation. Without exchanging a word, he spurred his horse, leveled his spear, and charged straight at Sheng Ben. Both armies raised a battle cry, and Sheng Ben leveled his spear and urged his horse forward to meet him. After the two generals had fought for more than ten bouts, Hu Sanniang spurred forward, brandishing her saber, to help her husband in the fray. Unable to withstand both opponents, Sheng Ben wheeled his horse and fled. Hu Sanniang galloped after him, overtook him, and with a sweep of her saber cut Sheng Ben down from his horse. Wang Ying and the others drove their troops forward in a sweeping attack. Ye Qing dared not resist and hurriedly withdrew with his men and horses. The Song troops pursued, killing more than five hundred soldiers, while the rest scattered and fled. Ye Qing escaped with only a little over one hundred horsemen and reached a place twenty li south of Xiangyuan city. Qiongying’s army had already arrived there and pitched camp.

p.src: The banner before the woman general’s horse bore the words plainly: “Vanguard General for the Pacification of the South, the Commandery Princess Qiongying.” When the officers of the southern army saw it, every one of them cheered. In both armies, painted alligator-hide drums thundered to the heavens, while multicolored embroidered banners filled the eye. Wang Ying, the “Stumpy Tiger,” saw that she was a beautiful woman. Spurring out from his lines, he leveled his spear and charged straight at Qiongying. As both armies raised a battle cry, Qiongying urged on her horse, twirled her halberd, and met him. After the two had fought for more than ten bouts, Wang the Stumpy Tiger could no longer rein in his lustful fancies, and his spearwork fell into disorder. Qiongying thought, “What a loathsome wretch!” She spied an opening and, with a single thrust of her halberd, struck Wang Ying in the left thigh. Wang Ying’s feet kicked at empty air, his helmet slipped backward over his head, and he crashed from his horse. Seeing her husband wounded, Hu Sanniang cursed, “You thieving, shameless little slut! How dare you behave so insolently!” She galloped out to rescue Wang Ying. Qiongying leveled her halberd and engaged her in combat. Wang Ying struggled on the ground but could not rise. Northern troops swarmed forward to seize him, but from the other side Sun Xin and Gu Dasao both rushed out and fought desperately to bring him back to their lines. Seeing that Hu Sanniang could not overcome Qiongying, Gu Dasao wielded her twin swords, spurred forward, and joined the fight. Three women generals, six arms, four steel swords, and one painted halberd met and clashed on horseback. It was like jade dust whirled by the wind and jeweled blossoms scattered through snow; the soldiers in both armies stared until their eyes were dazzled. After the three women had fought for more than twenty bouts, Qiongying feinted with an empty thrust, then trailed her halberd, wheeled her horse, and fled. Hu Sanniang and Gu Dasao pursued her together. Qiongying held the painted halberd in her left hand and took a stone in her right. Twisting her slender waist and glancing sideways with her bright eyes, she took careful aim at Hu Sanniang and sent the stone flying, striking her squarely on the right wrist. Overcome by pain, Hu Sanniang dropped one of her swords, wheeled her horse, and returned to her own lines. When Gu Dasao saw Hu Sanniang struck, she abandoned the pursuit of Qiongying and went to her aid. Qiongying reined about and came after them. Enraged, Sun Xin brandished his twin whips and charged forward on horseback. Before they could cross weapons, Qiongying had already sent a stone flying. With a clang, it struck squarely upon his bronze lion helmet. Sun Xin was greatly alarmed and dared not advance. He hurried back to his lines, protected Wang Ying and Hu Sanniang, and withdrew with his troops.

p.src: Just as Qiongying was about to drive her troops in pursuit, a sudden cannon blast rang out. It was near the end of the second month: the willow tips thrashed like disordered banners, and beyond the blossoms horses neighed again and again. A body of troops burst from behind the hillside. They were Lin Chong, Sun An, and the infantry chiefs Li Kui and the others, sent by Song Gongming’s command to bring support. The two armies collided, drums thundered, banners waved, and cries of battle rose ceaselessly from both formations. From that side, Lin Chong, the “Panther Head,” sat foremost on his horse with his eighteen-foot serpent spear leveled. From this side, Qiongying, the “Jade Arrowhead,” twirled her square-bladed painted halberd and galloped forward. Seeing that his opponent was a woman, Lin Chong shouted, “You vile wench! How dare you resist the armies of Heaven!” Qiongying made no reply. Twirling her halberd, she spurred her horse and charged straight at Lin Chong. Lin Chong leveled his spear and met her. The two horses crossed, and both weapons rose together. After countless bouts, Qiongying could no longer withstand him. She offered an opening, feinted with her halberd, then wheeled her horse and fled eastward. Lin Chong galloped after her. At the southern lines, Sun An recognized Qiongying’s banner and cried, “General Lin, do not pursue her! I fear some hidden trick!” But Lin Chong was supremely skilled and would not listen. Spurring his horse, he pressed close behind her. Across the lush green turf, the eight hooves flew like tumbling cups and clashing cymbals, racing with a thunderous clatter like balls of wind. When Qiongying saw that Lin Chong had drawn near, she raised the painted halberd lightly in her left hand, reached into her embroidered pouch with her right, and drew out a stone. Twisting around, she judged the distance to Lin Chong’s face and sent the stone flying. Sharp-eyed and quick-handed, Lin Chong knocked the stone aside with the shaft of his spear. Seeing that she had missed, Qiongying took up a second stone. When her hand rose, it was truly like a shooting star and a flash of lightning; the stone came with such fearful force that ghosts would wail and spirits tremble, flying once more at Lin Chong. Lin Chong could not dodge in time. The stone struck his face, sending fresh blood spurting forth, and he trailed his spear as he retreated to his lines. Qiongying reined about and pursued him.

p.src: Sun An was just about to advance when the soldiers in his formation parted to open a way. Five hundred infantrymen rushed out through the middle, led by five fierce generals well practiced in fighting on foot: Li Kui, Lu Zhishen, Wu Song, Xie Zhen, and Xie Bao. Gripping his broad axes, Li Kui charged straight toward her and shouted, “You woman, cease your insolence!” Seeing how fiercely he approached, Qiongying took a stone and hurled it at Li Kui, striking him squarely on the brow. Li Kui too was startled, but fortunately his hide was tough and his bones hard: the blow hurt him, yet broke neither skin nor bone. Seeing that she could not bring Li Kui down, Qiongying galloped back into her formation. Li Kui flew into a rage. His tiger whiskers bristled, his strange eyes opened round, and with a tremendous roar he charged straight into the enemy ranks. Fearing that Li Kui might come to harm, Lu Zhishen, Wu Song, Xie Zhen, and Xie Bao all charged forward together. How could Sun An possibly hold them back? When Qiongying saw them pursuing, she cast another stone and at once knocked Xie Zhen to the ground. Xie Bao, Lu Zhishen, and Wu Song hurried over to support and rescue him. Meanwhile Li Kui thought only of pursuit. When Qiongying saw him draw near, she hurriedly sent another stone flying and struck him once more on the brow. Only after being struck twice did fresh blood begin to gush forth. Yet Li Kui was an iron man to the end. Bright red blood ran over his dark face, but he still raged like fire, swinging both axes as he burst into the formation and hacked the northern troops into disorder. On the other side, when Sun An saw Qiongying enter the formation, he rallied his soldiers and charged in. Just then Wu Li arrived with Xu Wei and eight other principal and subordinate officers, leading the main army, and the two sides fell into a confused melee. Meanwhile Lu Zhishen and Wu Song, having rescued Xie Zhen, turned and fought their way into the northern formation. Xie Bao was supporting his elder brother and could not fight properly. Northern soldiers overtook them and cast entangling ropes, dragging both Xie Zhen and Xie Bao sprawling to the ground and hauling them into their formation as prisoners. The infantry suffered a crushing defeat and fled back. Sun An, however, fought on with heroic ferocity and, with a single stroke of his sword, cut the northern general Tang Xian from his horse. Wu Li was struck in the neck by an arrow shot from concealment by one of Sun An’s soldiers and tumbled from his horse. Xu Wei and the others fought desperately to rescue him and lift him back into the saddle.

p.src: Early the next morning, the soldiers reported that there was still no trace or word of Lu Zhishen.
